feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. It is the iteration 1 design (best raced score 158.144) with two changes: the outer sensors return to x = ±0.04 (the iteration 1 layout), and kp rises from 3.0 to 3.5. Iteration 3 showed that widening the outer sensors to ±0.06 lowered the score to 54.87 and removed all oval finishes (5/20 to 0/20), so H2 is rejected and the iteration 1 layout is the only one with evidence of oval finishes. kp has not been tested alone, but the iteration 1 telemetry shows max_error of about 0.061 to 0.063 m on every track with low steering oscillation (0.15 to 0.22), which points to drift on bends that a stronger proportional correction could address. The candidate is valid: all values are inside the contract ranges, and kp 3.5 is well inside the 0 to 20 limit. Its one change from the best raced design is a single-variable test, so it is worth racing now to learn whether kp is the lever. Approve it. After the race, check progress and max_error on s-bend and slalom, then steering_oscillation and line_loss_events. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, the next lever is kd (for example 0.5 at kp 3.5) rather than more kp. If progress on s-bend and slalom is unchanged or lower than iteration 1 (about 0.17 and 0.11), kp is not the main limit, and the next test should be a seven-sensor layout that adds x = ±0.04 at a finer pitch, not further gain changes. If the oval finish rate rises above 0.25, keep kp 3.5 and tune kd.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 with kp 3.5, keep the iteration 1 sensor layout and try kd 0.5 at kp 3.5, since iteration 1 showed low oscillation (0.15 to 0.22) and so jitter is not yet the limit.

If progress on s-bend and slalom stays at or below the iteration 1 levels (about 0.17 and 0.11) with max_error still near 0.06 m, do not raise kp further. Try a seven-sensor layout that keeps x = ±0.04 and adds inner sensors at a finer pitch (for example x = ±0.03), since iteration 3 showed that outer-only widening does not help.

If the oval finish rate is at least 0.25 and progress on bends rises, keep kp 3.5 and hold the other fields, then consider a small base_speed increase to about 1.7 only if completion_time stays well under 3.0 s. Do not lower base_speed, because iteration 2 showed that 1.2 costs oval finishes.
